title: Synchronized embedded desingularization with intrinsic ambient comparison
statement:
Work over $\mathbf Q$. Consider all closed immersions $X\hookrightarrow P$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $X$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and $P$ a smooth separated finite-type scheme, including finite disjoint unions of such pairs [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exists an embedded resolution algorithm $E$ with a common totally ordered set of synchronization labels. It assigns to each pair a finite ordinary blowup tower $P_r\to\cdots\to P_0=P$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], retaining its centers $C_i\hookrightarrow P_i$, and the successive scheme-theoretic strict transforms $X_i\hookrightarrow P_i$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Each $C_i$ is contained in $X_i$, is nonempty, regular, and nowhere dense in $X_i$, and has coherent ideal on $P_i$ and on $X_i$ [pqf-def-coherent]; $X_r$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The tower is stopped when $X_i$ is regular; no subsequent exceptional-divisor cleanup is included. A closed subscheme is nowhere dense if its underlying closed set contains no nonempty open subset of the ambient scheme in question. Each stage has a distinct label, and the labels occur in the common prescribed order. The empty input and a regular $X$ have the empty tower.

For every smooth morphism $v:Q\to P$ between the indicated ambient schemes, the algorithm on $X\times_P Q\hookrightarrow Q$ is the pullback of the embedded tower, deleting precisely empty centers and retaining their labels; identities and compositions give the same labeled comparisons. No constant relative dimension is required. A label absent from a restricted tower denotes an empty center and an identity stage.

If the same reduced $X$ is closed embedded in two such ambient schemes, the two labeled towers of strict transforms of $X$, together with their ideal centers on those strict transforms, are canonically identified over $X$, with exactly the same labels. These intrinsic comparisons also respect isomorphisms of $X$ and are transitive for three embeddings. Here labels encode the invariant synchronization, not consecutive stage numbers renumbered independently on each component or open subset.

source.place: Expose VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, printed pp.93--94: the strong Bierstone--Milman algorithm and the invariant synchronization correction of Bierstone--Milman--Temkin, Q-universal desingularization (2011), Theorem 6.1, Addendum and section 6.3. This embedded, labeled input is stated separately; the detailed reference is WANTED, not claimed to have been read. No Stacks tag supplies embedded resolution.

proof.text: Use the corrected local invariant $\nu_H$ of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-resolution-invariant-calculus]. Starting with the empty ambient history, if $X_i$ is regular, stop. Otherwise take $m_i=\max\nu_{H_i}>\bot$, give this stage the label $m_i$, and put $C_i=M_{H_i}$. Form the ordinary ambient blowup and its scheme-theoretic strict transform. Clause (1) gives precisely the asserted properties of $C_i$ and says that the next pair is again in the allowed class. The maximum value strictly decreases whenever a next nonterminal stage exists. Give the common label set $V\setminus\{\bot\}$ the reverse of its invariant order. Thus labels in every constructed tower are distinct and occur in the same prescribed order. For the empty scheme there is no positive maximum, so the recursion stops immediately; it also stops immediately for every regular input. Apply the same rule to a finite disjoint union, taking its maximum over the entire union, rather than renumbering its components independently.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, pp.93--94; BMT 6.1 Addendum and 6.3: build the tower from full maximum loci, with corrected synchronization.

proof.text: This recursion is exactly the maximum-stratum process of clause (4) of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-resolution-invariant-calculus], for the same functions $\nu_H$ used in Step 1. Hence it stops after finitely many blowups. At its last stage there is no positive invariant value: otherwise clause (1) of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-resolution-invariant-calculus] would give the next nonempty center, contradicting termination. That same clause says that every local ring of $X_r$ is regular, so $X_r$ is regular. Since the recursion is defined to stop at this first regular stage, it omits the exceptional-divisor cleanup described in ILO 2.3.11. No well-foundedness of an arbitrary ordered label set is being assumed.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11, p.93: stop the strong algorithm when the strict transform is smooth; termination supplied separately by the maximum-process input.

proof.text: Fix a smooth ambient map $v:Q\to P$ and the finite labeled tower just constructed over $P$. Its ambient pullbacks are ordinary blowups: $v$ is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], with the comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], identifies each pulled-back stage with the blowup of the extended center ideal. The maps from the pulled-back ambient schemes and strict transforms to their originals are base changes of $v$, hence smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. To see scheme-theoretic equality of the strict transforms at the next stage, apply [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed] to $X_i\hookrightarrow P_i$ and to its pullback: both strict transforms are the intrinsic blowups of these closed subschemes in the corresponding center ideals. Flat blowup base change identifies these intrinsic blowups as well. This proves the required cartesian identifications inductively; no assertion that mere topological closure commutes with pullback is used.

source.place: VIII 2.1.4 and 2.3.4; ordinary blowup and strict-transform calculus, using the existing generic scheme-theoretic comparison statements.

proof.text: Induct through the ordered labels of the tower over $P$. Suppose that the algorithm over $Q$ has so far performed exactly the nonempty pulled-back centers of the earlier labels. At the current history, clause (2) of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-resolution-invariant-calculus] identifies the invariant on the pulled-back strict transform with the pulled-back invariant on $X_i$, and identifies the center ideals. If the stratum with label $m_i$ has nonempty inverse image, then $m_i$ is also the maximum value there: all its values are at most $m_i$ and some equal it. The rule of Step 1 therefore selects exactly this pulled-back center as the next center over $Q$, with the same label. If its inverse image is empty, clause (2) says its ideal is the unit ideal, so this is an identity stage and changes neither the strict transform nor its local invariant; skip it. After all labels over $P$ have been inspected, the pulled-back final history has invariant $\bot$ everywhere, again by clause (2), and is regular by clause (1). Thus there are no additional stages over $Q$. This proves deletion of precisely the empty centers, including the case that $Q$ only meets the regular locus. The invariant comparison expressly allows the relative dimension to vary.

source.place: VIII 2.3.4, 2.3.5(i)--(ii), 2.3.13; BMT 6.3: induction comparing maximum values, with empty stages retained as labels.

proof.text: Now fix two ambient embeddings of the same $X$. At stage zero the intrinsic histories agree. If their histories through the preceding label agree, clause (3) of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-resolution-invariant-calculus] says the invariant functions, their maxima, and their reduced center ideals on the identified strict transforms agree. Their next labels and centers on those strict transforms are consequently identical. By [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed], each next strict transform is the blowup of this same intrinsic scheme in this same ideal. Identify them by that common blowup, retaining the center ideal and its place in the history. Induction gives the asserted intrinsic comparison at every label. They stop simultaneously because regularity is detected by $\nu_H=\bot$. This argument compares the strict-transform towers; it does not identify the two different ambient blowup schemes.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; BMT 6.1 Addendum (3), 6.3, paragraph on independence of the local embedding variety.

proof.text: For a smooth identity map, extending the ideal does nothing and every nonempty label is retained. The identity is smooth, and composites are smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. For composable smooth maps $R\xrightarrow{w}Q\xrightarrow{v}P$, the center ideal at any retained label is obtained by two successive extensions of scalars; this is the same ideal as extension along $vw$, since the generators of either ideal are the images of the same original local sections. A center empty on $Q$ remains empty on $R$. A center nonempty on $Q$ but empty on $R$ is removed at the second restriction, just as in direct restriction. The comparisons of Step 3 all arise from the same blowup of these identical ideals, so the stage identifications coincide. This proves the identity and composition assertions, including their labels.

source.place: VIII 2.3.4 and the ordinary blowup comparison; elementary compatibility once the centers and their extended ideals have been identified.

proof.text: Finally, an isomorphism of initial reduced schemes identifies their invariant histories by clause (3) of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-resolution-invariant-calculus]. Repeating the induction of Step 5 therefore compares the intrinsic towers along this isomorphism. For three embeddings, all three pairwise comparisons at the next stage are the maps induced by the identity on the same intrinsic scheme and its same center ideal; both composites are that identity-induced map on its blowup. Starting at $X$, induction proves transitivity at all stages. The same observation shows that these intrinsic comparisons agree with restriction or smooth ambient pullback, since clause (3) commutes with those operations and the extended ideals are equal. The comparisons are canonical at the level of the labeled blowups of ideals, even if an individual blowup morphism is an identity.

source.place: BMT 6.1 Addendum (3)--(4) and 6.3; intrinsic invariant and ideal comparisons, with cocycle checked stage by stage.

proof_origin.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; construction from the separate local invariant calculus and termination inputs. Detailed BMT archival source WANTED; online arXiv:0905.3580 sections 6.1--6.3 read.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q44-73173d966 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 7 steps, both new nodes, every cited statement, the parent's use of the item, and ILO VIII 2.2.7-2.3.17 (pp.90-95). BMT is not in literature/ (WANTED), so its content is judged only through ILO's account of it. The item statement is unchanged. It matches ILO 2.3.10/2.3.11, restricted to embedded finite-type Q-schemes, with the conventions of 2.3.1 and 2.3.4-2.3.5 and the synchronization fix of 2.3.13 (BMT 6.3). It keeps centres in Sing, stops at the first regular stage without cleanup, and its labels survive smooth pullback even when relative dimension varies. Step checks: Step 1 uses clause (1): centres are nonempty, regular, nowhere dense and coherent, and the maximum strictly drops. Step 3 uses flat blowup base change (lem-pc-smooth-flat, thm/def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change, lem-pc-proper-base-change (2)) and Bl_C(X_i) = strict transform (lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed); the argument is scheme-theoretic. Step 4: the induction over P's stages is right; when the inverse image is nonempty, the maximum over Q is m_i, an empty stratum gives a unit-ideal stage that is deleted, and the tower ends with nu = bottom. Step 5: the intrinsic histories agree by clause (3), and the next strict transform is the same intrinsic blowup. Step 6: extension of ideals composes. Step 7: blowup automorphisms are trivial, which gives the cocycle. Small cases tested: xy=0 in A^2 and A^3, (xy=0)xA^1, an open missing the node, a surface plus a nodal curve, and the empty scheme. A normalized invariant is required because raw Hilbert-Samuel functions are not invariant under a smooth factor or across dimensions; the node states this. There is no duplicate in the DAG; the only Hilbert-Samuel hits are dimension-theory nodes. Fault (B2/B3, interface): the calculus node only gives the existence of nu ('the BM construction supplies...'), and no node defines that construction. The termination node then claims termination for 'the' nu. Read that way, it is either an unsourced claim about any nu with (1)-(3), or a claim about an undefined object, which stage 2 would have to pick by choice (hollow data). FIX: the calculus node now says there exist one ordered V and functions nu_H, for all pairs and histories, with properties (1)-(4), where clause (4) is the termination statement with the same process and edge cases. The termination node is dropped, item Step 2 cites clause (4) for the same nu, and proof_deps and the summary are updated. The item statement is unchanged. Accepted tool_uses: lem-pc-smooth-flat, thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change, lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed and lem-pc-proper-base-change, as generic blowup and smooth-base-change black boxes. No SGA is cited.; 2 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
